quiz.title: Class 1 Logical Reasoning Quiz
quiz.intro: Eight friendly reasoning questions on patterns, odd-one-out, sequences, sorting and simple analogies. Read each one with your child, pick an answer, then press Check my score.

questions.q: A pattern goes triangle, circle, triangle, circle, triangle, and then ___. What shape comes next?
questions.explanation: The shapes take turns: triangle, circle, triangle, circle. After a triangle it is always a circle’s turn.

questions.q: Which one is the odd one out: cat, apple, dog, cow?
questions.explanation: Cat, dog and cow are animals. Apple is a fruit, so it does not belong with the others.
The numbers jump by 2 each time: 2, 4, 6, 8, so the next one is 8 + 2 = 10.

questions.q: Which of these belongs in a group of things you can eat?
questions.explanation: A banana is food you can eat. A ball, a shoe and a book are not, so the banana is the one that fits the group.

questions.q: Big is to small as tall is to ___?
questions.explanation: Big and small are opposites. The opposite of tall is short, so tall goes with short.

questions.q: Look at this growing pattern: 1 star, 2 stars, 3 stars, ___ stars. How many stars come next?
questions.explanation: Each step adds one more star: 1, 2, 3, so the next step has 3 + 1 = 4 stars.

questions.q: Count backward: 10, 9, 8, ___. What number comes next?
questions.explanation: Counting backward means one less each time: 10, 9, 8, so the next number is 8 − 1 = 7.

questions.q: Three of these shapes have straight sides and corners. Which one is different: square, triangle, rectangle, circle?
questions.explanation: A square, a triangle and a rectangle all have straight sides and corners. A circle is round with no corners, so it is the odd one out.

faq.q: What is logical reasoning for Class 1?
faq.a: It is simple thinking practice for 6 to 7 year olds — spotting patterns, finding the odd one out, continuing number sequences, sorting things into groups, and matching simple opposites. The maths is easy on purpose; the skill being built is careful noticing.

faq.q: Why should a Grade 1 child practise reasoning and not just sums?
faq.a: Reasoning teaches a child to look for the rule behind a question rather than guess. That habit makes addition, word problems and later maths far less confusing, because the child already asks ‘what is the pattern here?’

faq.q: How do I help my child with a pattern question?
faq.a: Read the pattern out loud together and let the child say it back with you. Hearing ‘triangle, circle, triangle, circle’ makes the missing part almost obvious. Point to each item as you say it so the eye and voice move together.

faq.q: How much reasoning practice is enough at this age?
faq.a: A few questions a day is plenty — about five to ten minutes. Short and regular beats a long session once a week, and it keeps a young child curious instead of tired.
